To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
molyb-denum limitation of nitrogen fixation is common in tropical forests and that this may limit the ability of some tropical forests to acquire new N in response to CO₂ fertilization.

1) Molybdenum is the only nutrient that consistently stimulates nitrogen fixation in tropical soil microcosms and intact forest plots, 2) Molybdeunum is the only limiting nutrient in the nitrogen fixation response to phosphorus fertilizer in microcosms, and 3) Molybdeenum is a contaminant of commercial phosphorus fertilizers.
molyb-denum (Mo) is an important factor in limiting nitrogen fixation in tropical soils.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of nitrogen in the tropical forest ecosystem and its response to global change.
the role of biological nitrogen fixation in the global carbon cycle.
the role of nitrogen-fixing bacteria in tropical forest ecosystems.

the micronutrients molybdenium and vanadium, which are both cofactors in the enzyme nitrogenase, are the limiting factor in biological nitrogen fixation in soils of tropical forests.
the micronutrients molybdenumb and phosphorus are the main limiting factors for the biological nitrogen fixation in the tropical forests.
